Customer -> provide 3 representative workload traces and target QPS/latency numbers (Samir) by 2026-11-05
Schedule a 2-hour benchmark window with Verdigris test dataset (Liam + Samir) for week of 2026-11-15

Liam Ortega: Prepare benchmark harness and test plan (due 2026-11-10)

header: Date: 2026-10-29 - Start: 15:00 UTC - Duration: 54m - Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Ortega (Redwood SE); Anita Rao (Verdigris Head of Product); Diego Martinez (Verdigris Security Lead); Samir Patel (Verdigris Cloud)
summary: POC scoping call to align on pilot success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks, and security/compliance gates (SOC 2/ISO, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logging). Discussed timeline for pilot, required artifacts, and a candidate benchmark window. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send doc pack and test harness; Verdigris to provide traces and compliance contacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 45-60 minutes, try to capture action items. um quick intros please
[00:12] Anita Rao: Anita here, head of product at Verdigris, leading this AI pilot, thanks Maya
[00:18] Diego Martinez: Diego, security lead. we'll be gating on SOC2 and encryption, mostly in charge of compliance review
[00:25] Samir Patel: Samir, infra, i'll own traces and run the benchmark servers on our side
[00:31] Liam Ortega: Liam, SE with Redwood, i'll take the benchmark plan and sizing questions. nice to meet you all
[00:38] Maya Chen: awesome, quick context: Verdigris wants a pilot to replace an internal NLU service for customer routing. goal is 80% reduction in latency p50 and cost neutrality vs current infra and safe controls for customer data. does that sound right Anita?
[00:53] Anita Rao: yeah that's accurate. also timelines: execs want a POC report by end of Q4, so roughly 6 weeks. we have strict data residency and need audit logs for interactions.
[01:07] Diego Martinez: and SOC 2 is non-negotiable for production but for pilot we need evidence: SOC 2 report, ISO certs, pen test summary, and SAML SSO for RBAC testing.
[01:20] Maya Chen: understood. we can provide SOC 2 attestation and ISO27001 summary, plus our SAML metadata and RBAC examples. i'll send those today.
[01:29] Anita Rao: great. can we walk through what success looks like? what metrics should the pilot prove?
[01:36] Liam Ortega: we typically propose success criteria that cover performance, cost, and quality. concrete examples: throughput target (qps), p50/p95 latency under expected batching, token cost per 1k responses, and NLU intent accuracy delta within +/- 2% of baseline.
[01:55] Samir Patel: for our volumetrics, our peak is around 250 qps with bursts to 600 for short windows, average payload about 600 tokens. is that high?
[02:05] Liam Ortega: that's a decent profile. for that we need to know concurrency and concurrency shaping policies. Redwood can run on hosted but for these bursts dedicated capacity or private is recommended to avoid cold start variability.
[02:18] Diego Martinez: on dedicated vs hosted, our compliance team prefers VPC / private model. can your private deployment run inside our VPC? and can we leverage KMS?
[02:29] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed into customer VPC or on-prem where you control KMS/HSM. For pilot we can start with Dedicated with TLS + customer-managed keys if needed. I'll loop the deployment docs.
[02:41] Anita Rao: timeline risk: if private deploy takes longer, can we fall back to hosted for the benchmark and still meet the exec date?
[02:49] Liam Ortega: yes, we can run an initial benchmark on hosted with synthetic data and then validate on dedicated/VPC later; metrics are comparable but you'll see slight diffs in latency. we recommend running final acceptance test in the same environment you plan to prod in.
[03:04] Anita Rao: ok, makes sense. what about security gates? Diego, do you want to outline your must-haves?
[03:10] Diego Martinez: sure. must-haves: SOC 2 type II report, ISO27001 cert, SSO via SAML or OIDC (SAML preferred), RBAC with audit logs for every API action, at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys, network controls (private IPs, peering), and retention policy for logs and request payloads. Also need an incident response playbook and a place to view audit trails.
[03:33] Maya Chen: we have all of those. our audit logs include token-level traces (redacted) and API-level logs with request IDs. retention policies configurable in Redwood Console and can be exported to your SIEM.
[03:46] Liam Ortega: to add, for pilot we can set up a reduced retention window or forward logs directly to your S3/Splunk. All of our RBAC roles are pluggable with SAML group mapping.
[03:58] Samir Patel: what's the expected artifacts you'll send over? we'll need to pass them to our risk team.
[04:03] Maya Chen: i'll send a single doc pack: SOC2 attestation, ISO summary, pen test summary, SAML integration guide, RBAC example configs, and a link to our audit log schema — aiming to send by Monday 2026-11-02.
[04:15] Anita Rao: excellent. Benchmarks: Liam what does your test plan look like?
[04:19] Liam Ortega: plan is: 1) ingest Verdigris traces (3 representative traces you provide), 2) run synthetic traffic to hit steady-state qps and burst windows, 3) measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, token cost, and quality metrics (intent accuracy). We'll run several iterations with different batch sizes and quantization settings.
[04:36] Samir Patel: we can extract traces from our gateway — will include headers, avg tokens, and concurrency. are there specific trace formats you prefer?
[04:42] Liam Ortega: JSONL with request/response timestamps is easiest; include payload size and any prompt templates. anonymize PII; we can also sign an NDA if you need.
[04:52] Diego Martinez: is model caching a thing? we need to understand how long embeddings or KV cache might persist between calls, for data retention concerns.
[04:58] Liam Ortega: Redwood uses KV cache for generation speedups; cache lifetime is configurable and can be disabled for regulated workloads. We'll document default cache behavior and how to purge.
[05:08] Anita Rao: what's the expected time to spin up a test cluster for the benchmark if we use dedicated?
[05:12] Maya Chen: for dedicated it's typically 5-7 business days once contracts and billing are set; private (VPC) can be 2-3 weeks depending on network approvals. Hosted is immediate.
[05:23] Samir Patel: 2-3 weeks for VPC is ok if we can at least run hosted initial tests.
[05:27] Liam Ortega: agreed. We'll do hosted first then an acceptance run in dedicated/vpc.
[05:31] Anita Rao: on success criteria, can we make acceptance gates binary? ex: P95 <= 450ms, P50 <= 120ms, token cost <= $X per 1k, intent accuracy delta <= 2%?
[05:44] Liam Ortega: yes we can draft that. We'll include a quality regression test suite that runs over your sample prompts and measures intent extraction and misclassification rate.
[05:53] Diego Martinez: for the audit trail, we need immutable logs with request id and user id mapping. will Redwood preserve those without modification?
[06:01] Maya Chen: yes, logs are append-only. We can forward via secure syslog or S3 with immutability configs on your side. We redact sensitive fields by default but can provide raw logs under strict access if needed for the pilot.
[06:14] Anita Rao: what's your policy on data residency — can requests and logs be kept in eu-west-1 only?
[06:20] Maya Chen: yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have region-aware routing but need to confirm residency guarantees; we'll include details in the doc pack.
[06:33] Diego Martinez: compliance review: we may need a short security workshop with your engineers to validate SAML, key handling, and audit log flow. Can we schedule that?
[06:41] Maya Chen: absolutely. suggest a 60–90 minute technical review the week after you get the doc pack. Liam will run the workshop.
[06:50] Anita Rao: timeline recap: we need report by end of Q4. With the send of docs on 11/02, workload traces by 11/05, benchmark window mid-Nov, and final acceptance by 12/15 is that realistic?
[07:03] Liam Ortega: that maps. Proposed schedule: 11/02 docs, 11/05 traces, 11/15 benchmark window, 11/22 run final acceptance in dedicated, 12/10 deliver report, 12/15 buffer.
[07:17] Samir Patel: 11/15 works for us for the perf window. we'll reserve infra and notify our SREs.
[07:22] Diego Martinez: one more question on SAML: we use Okta and enforce SCIM group sync. can Redwood map Okta groups to RBAC roles and accept SCIM?
[07:33] Liam Ortega: yes for SAML group mapping. SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync; we'll include sample manifests.
[07:41] Anita Rao: pricing question: what will the pilot cost estimate look like? we want a ballpark to budget for Dedicated capacity during the benchmark window.
[07:49] Maya Chen: we'll include a pilot estimate line item in the doc pack. Quick back-of-envelope for 250 qps steady: depends on model size/quantization; ballpark dedicated hourly for the cluster plus token costs — we'll provide a spreadsheet.
[08:04] Anita Rao: ok. any risks we haven't covered?
[08:07] Samir Patel: network egress and peering approvals might slow VPC setup.
[08:12] Diego Martinez: compliance signoff may require legal review of our DPA — we should share that early.
[08:17] Maya Chen: we'll attach our DPA and standard SOC2 artifact list.
[08:21] Liam Ortega: technical note — for accuracy comparisons we'll need to freeze model version and prompt templates; changing both mid-run invalidates comparisons.
[08:30] Anita Rao: understood. let's freeze templates for the benchmark.
[08:34] Maya Chen: recap of next steps and owners: i'll send doc pack and pricing, Liam will prep benchmark harness, Samir provide traces, Diego confirm compliance stakeholders. schedule the technical workshop for week of 11/08.
[08:49] Anita Rao: sounds good. thanks everyone
[08:52] Diego Martinez: thanks
[08:54] Liam Ortega: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the plan.
[08:57] Maya Chen: thanks, meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present; some product names may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache spelled as 'K-V cash' in sections). Links shared during call: https://redwood.example/soc2.pdf, https://redwood.example/saml-guide.pdf, shared spreadsheet: https://redwood.example/pilot-costs.xlsx
